structural_base_plate.why_room_owned: the shared library has no base plate; the reference room main_room_02/v003 keeps the same floor/floor_base package (object FLOOR_BASE, 0.26 thick). Its top face is what shows through the 60 mm grout between the 5 m tile modules.

door_wall_origin_note: common_components origin = wall centreline, so slots sit at +-7.35 and the wall occupies 7.2..7.5, the same occupancy the runtime gets by putting its door-wall node at the outer face 7.5

open_issues.detail: common_components wall_door_5m lintel is 9.4m tall (local z 2.5..11.9), so the opening runs 0..2.5 from the wall base. With the walkable floor top at z=0.30 the usable clear height is 2.2m, while whitebox v003 door_contract specifies bottom_z 0.30 + height 2.5 (clear 2.5m, lintel 9.1m tall). 0.30m disagreement between the shared component library and the whitebox contract; the library was used unmodified (GLB is visual-only) and Godot owns the opening.
open_issues.owner: common_components v004 or whitebox contract revision

open_issues.detail: whitebox v003 authored the south doorway on slot centre +2.5 (south wall = 2.5 trim + 5 solid + 5 door + 2.5 trim) and no east doorway. The runtime puts both doorways in the middle 5m slot and the 5m shared component cannot represent a 2.5m trim, so v007 follows the runtime.

the authored west wall ran a 2.9 m panel cadence across the whole 15 m wall and the authored south / east armour was drawn around the OLD door positions (south 4+2 panels, east 5 panels, none slot-aligned). All three now take the shared component unit (2x2.4 m panel + cap per 5 m slot), so the panel count changes: west 5 -> 12, south 6 -> 8, east 10 -> 8. North is verbatim (12 -> 12). This is the price of "one unit, no direction".

the room authored the 4 c02 floor tiles in two variants: 21+32 carry the square access cover, 12+23 do not. The generic component takes the WITH-cover variant, so FLOORSLOT_R01_C02 and FLOORSLOT_R02_C03 gain a cover (4 extra parts each). The tile structural frame (4 edge trims + 2 blue seams) is identical on all 9 tiles and is the part the alignment claim rests on.
open_issues.owner: art review; cosmetic, no gameplay effect

open_issues.detail: each authored tile carried its own unique scuff decals (地砖磨损). A generic component keeps one representative set per variant, so the same scuffs repeat on all 5 c01 tiles. Deliberate: per-tile uniqueness cannot survive "one unit serves every slot". If per-tile variation is wanted back it has to be a decal layer in Godot, not baked into the tile component.

measured encroachments into the exact 2.2 x 2.5 opening, none of them blocking (the hard CORE gate is empty; Godot owns the opening, the door FSM, navigation and collision, and the GLB is visual only). Both doorways carry the same set, all inherited from v003 art: the shared floor tile (r01_c02 / r02_c03) raises its decorative inlay 41 mm proud of the 0.30 walkable surface at the threshold; the gate frame LED strips muzzle 17.5 mm into the clear width on each side (the opening is 2.2 m nominal, 2.165 m between strips); the wall-base trim bar crosses the threshold 7 mm proud, and an east-wall inlay seam 9 mm. See doorway_edge_grazes_m for the full table.
open_issues.owner: art review; cosmetic, no gameplay effect

open_issues.detail: the shared library authors every wall/floor part at location (0,0,0) with its vertices already in the component root-local frame, parented to a ROOT_* empty that marks the library layout position. Canonicalising through that root offset double-counts it and displaces whole slots by tens of metres while every shape hash still agrees. The build now verifies the declared shape convention (STRUCTURAL body x/y centred on the origin, z from 0) and the final ring / grid world bounds, and qa/verify_entry_safe_room_v007.py re-measures the saved blend independently.
